note: Per-frame pose scripts for Zenitsu's v3 redraw (same conventions as tools/art_v3/poses/tanjiro.json). Frame counts, phase breaks and timing semantics match the shipped atlas. He fights ASLEEP: eyes closed, and the katana rests SHEATHED in every neutral pose; it is drawn only between an attack's startup and its recovery. Every clip uses wide 768x1024 columns: the iai stance and the scabbard behind him do not fit a 512 column. "stance": low-stance clips (QA band vs the idle); "upright_frames": frames that stand fully upright.

idle_key.intro: Correction of the chosen idle key pose (input image 1): the Thunder Breathing iai stance, eyes closed. Everything stays exactly as drawn except his two hands and the sword, which are redrawn so the sheathed katana is ONE straight line. Both columns are the same corrected drawing (two attempts).

His left hand holds the scabbard just behind the tsuba, thumb on the tsuba; his right hand grips the hilt just in front of the tsuba, ready to draw. No blade showing.

The same correction as frame 1: one straight sheathed katana from the scabbard tip behind him (left) to the pommel in front (right), left hand on the scabbard at the tsuba, right hand on the hilt in front of it, ready to draw; no blade showing.

walk.intro: In-place forward walk cycle in a LOW stance, still asleep: knees deeply bent, torso leaning forward, the katana stays SHEATHED on his left hip, left hand on the scabbard, right hand on the hilt, eyes closed. The top of his head is only about 10 percent higher than in input image 1 (never standing upright). Short gliding steps; torso, head and sword stay steady (at most 6 px of bob); the pelvis stays at the same X in every frame. It is a seamless loop, not a story of moving right.
frames: Contact: near leg reaches forward RIGHT with the heel touching the ground, far leg behind on its toes; low stance held.
Down: weight moves onto the near foot, both knees bend a little more, far heel lifts.
Passing: far foot glides forward close to the ground under the pelvis, near leg supports; body at its highest (still low).
Up: far foot travels ahead of the support foot, about to land.
Opposite contact: far leg now forward RIGHT with the heel down, near leg behind on its toes (the legs swapped compared with frame 1).
Opposite down: weight moves onto the far foot, knees bend a little more, near heel lifts.
Opposite passing: near foot glides forward under the pelvis, far leg supports; body at its highest (still low).
Opposite up: near foot travels ahead, about to land; flows directly into frame 1.

walk_back.intro: In-place backward walk cycle in the same LOW stance, still asleep (the katana stays SHEATHED on his left hip, left hand on the scabbard, right hand on the hilt, eyes closed).
